subject: Dealing with measurement invariance in an intervention study

messages.author: 2936e086c770a552
messages.subject: Dealing with measurement invariance in an intervention study
parts:
Hello out there,

I'm interested in the dependency of learning environments and it's assessment.
I applied randomly one of two different Likert-scales on measurement point (MP) 1 about the justification of scientific knowledge. Afterwards, I applied randomly one of two different learning environments to foster views about justifying of scientific knowledge. On MP 2, the participant had the same scale as on MP 1.  

For this 2x2 design I want to assess measurement invariance. But I struggle with the step-up approach in testing measurement invariance.

My questions: 

Do I need to constrain the intercepts for the groups and both measurement points?

Recht_A_1 ~ T1*1
Recht_A_2 ~ T2*1
Recht_A_3 ~ T3*1
Recht_A_4 ~ T4*1
Recht_A_5 ~ T5*1
Recht_A_6 ~ T6*1
Recht_A_7 ~ T7*1

Recht_B_1 ~ T1*1
Recht_B_2 ~ T2*1
Recht_B_3 ~ T3*1
Recht_B_4 ~ T4*1
Recht_B_5 ~ T5*1
Recht_B_6 ~ T6*1
Recht_B_7 ~ T7*1

Or because I'm interested in mean differences, do I need to constrain the intercepts just for the groups?  

Recht_A_1 ~ T1*1
Recht_A_2 ~ T2*1
Recht_A_3 ~ T3*1
Recht_A_4 ~ T4*1
Recht_A_5 ~ T5*1
Recht_A_6 ~ T6*1
Recht_A_7 ~ T7*1

Recht_B_1 ~ T8*1
Recht_B_2 ~ T9*1
Recht_B_3 ~ T10*1
Recht_B_4 ~ T11*1
Recht_B_5 ~ T12*1
Recht_B_6 ~ T13*1
Recht_B_7 ~ T14*1

I'm not only interested in mean differences, but as well in the influence of covariate and outcomes (reading ability, learning disability or socio economic status). Thats why I want to apply SEM.

Many thanks in advance!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Dealing with measurement invariance in an intervention study
parts: For this 2x2 design I want to assess measurement invariance.

2 (random Likert scale) x 2 (random learning environment) x 2 (time points) pretest-posttest design.  So you have 4 groups and 2 occasions.  How do the scales differ?  Are the 2 scales supposed to be parallel forms?  That is, does it make sense to constrain loadings/intercepts from one scale to be equal to loadings/intercepts from the other scale?
Do I need to constrain the intercepts for the groups and both measurement points?

Yes, in order to compare latent means (right? you didn't specify) across all 8 contexts, it is necessary that the measurement parameters (loadings AND intercepts) are constrained across those contexts.  Given the experimental design (random assignment to 4 groups), I think you can start with a model that already imposes equality constraints at Time 1 because there is no reason to suspect those are different populations.  You can then further constrain the Time-2 measurement parameters to equal Time 1.  You could still test invariance by beginning with an unconstrained Time-1 measurement model, but it would be a less parsimonious baseline model to start with.

Recht_A_1 ~ c(T1, T1, T1, T1)*1
Recht_A_2 ~ c(T2, T2, T2, T2)*1
...

Recht_B_1 ~ c(T1, T1, T1, T1)*1
Recht_B_2 ~ c(T2, T2, T2, T2)*1
...

You need to specify a vector of labels to constrain parameters across groups (as I edited above).  Providing 1 label will only apply that label  to the first group.

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html
I'm not only interested in mean differences, but as well in the influence of covariate and outcomes (reading ability, learning disability or socio economic status).

That complicates things if you try to do everything in one model.  I would first try establishing invariance of the factor model with respect to your experimental groups and time.  If (at least partial) invariance holds, add covariate(s) predicting the factor to see if the model still fits well.  If not, then you may need to allow the covariate to directly affect at least one indicator as well as the factor, implying lack of measurement invariance with respect to that covariate (look up literature about MIMIC or Restricted Factor Analysis models for testing measurement invariance).  If you can establish (at least partial) invariance with respect to the covariate(s) as well, then add the outcome variable(s) as a predictive validity check.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Hey Terrence,

thank you for taking time!
Are the 2 scales supposed to be parallel forms?

Yes, the Likert-scale shall have the same construct. I changed wording (complex vs. easy language) and response format ("I agree...I disagress vs. star-rating) and provided once a read-aloud function.

Do I need to constrain the intercepts for the groups and both measurement points?

Yes, in order to compare latent means (right? you didn't specify) across all 8 contexts, it is necessary that the measurement parameters (loadings AND intercepts) are constrained across those contexts.

The following model (thanks for your advice) supports configural and weak invariance. Strong invariance is not supported. Now, I want to assess partial invariance.

model <-'
Recht1 =~ c(L1,L1,L1,L1)*Recht_A_1 + c(L2,L2,L2,L2)*Recht_A_2 + c(L3,L3,L3,L3)*Recht_A_3 + c(L4,L4,L4,L4)*Recht_A_4 + c(L5,L5,L5,L5)*Recht_A_5 + c(L6,L6,L6,L6)*Recht_A_6 + c(L7,L7,L7,L7)*Recht_A_7
Recht2 =~ c(L1,L1,L1,L1)*Recht_B_1 + c(L2,L2,L2,L2)*Recht_B_2 + c(L3,L3,L3,L3)*Recht_B_3 + c(L4,L4,L4,L4)*Recht_B_4 + c(L5,L5,L5,L5)*Recht_B_5 + c(L6,L6,L6,L6)*Recht_B_6 + c(L7,L7,L7,L7)*Recht_B_7

## correlate residuals of indicators with themselves across time
Recht_A_1~~Recht_B_1
Recht_A_2~~Recht_B_2  
Recht_A_3~~Recht_B_3  
Recht_A_4~~Recht_B_4
Recht_A_5~~Recht_B_5
Recht_A_6~~Recht_B_6  
Recht_A_7~~Recht_B_7
Recht_A_2~~Recht_B_3
Recht_A_3~~Recht_B_4

Recht1~~Recht1
Recht2~~Recht2
Recht1~~Recht2

Recht_A_1 ~ c(T1, T1, T1, T1)*1
Recht_A_2 ~ c(T2, T2, T2, T2)*1

Recht_A_3 ~ c(T3, T3, T3, T3)*1
Recht_A_4 ~ c(T4, T4, T4, T4)*1
Recht_A_5 ~ c(T5, T5, T5, T5)*1
Recht_A_6 ~ c(T6, T6, T6, T6)*1
Recht_A_7 ~ c(T7, T7, T7, T7)*1

Recht_B_1 ~ c(T1, T1, T1, T1)*1
Recht_B_2 ~ c(T2, T2, T2, T2)*1

Recht_B_3 ~ c(T3, T3, T3, T3)*1
Recht_B_4 ~ c(T4, T4, T4, T4)*1
Recht_B_5 ~ c(T5, T5, T5, T5)*1
Recht_B_6 ~ c(T6, T6, T6, T6)*1
Recht_B_7 ~ c(T7, T7, T7, T7)*1
'

I used the following functions
lavTestScore() 
and  
parTable()
according to this post.

It comes up, that the intercepts should be freed with a "freeing modifier" (NA or 1?):

Recht_B_1 ~ c(NA/1, T1, T1, T1)*1
Recht_B_2 ~ c(T2, T2, T2, T2)*1

Recht_B_3 ~ c(T3, T3, T3, T3)*1
Recht_B_4 ~ c(T4, T4, T4, T4)*1
Recht_B_5 ~ c(T5, NA/1, T5, T5)*1
Recht_B_6 ~ c(T6, T6, T6, NA/1)*1
Recht_B_7 ~ c(T7, T7, T7, T7)*1'

Unfortunately, this doesn't work in any way.

ERROR in lavaanify(model = FLAT, constraints = constraints, varTable = lavdata@ov,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: wrong number of arguments in modifier (T1,T1,T1) of element Recht_B_1~1

And just to be sure: 1) Is it allow to free an intercept for only one group in the second occasion? 2) If yes, how do code this?  
With regard to post I mentioned above, I would free the intercepts for every group in the second occasion.

Thanks in advance

messages.subject: Re: Dealing with measurement invariance in an intervention study
parts:
Is it allow to free an intercept for only one group in the second occasion? 2) If yes, how do code this?  
With regard to post I mentioned above, I would free the intercepts for every group in the second occasion.

You already figured out the syntax, but yes, you can free in just one group at the second occasion if that is what the data suggest.  You can think of this like a MANCOVA.  I don't know the order of your groups, but the interpretation of one freed intercept at Time 2 would be something like the following:

Given (controlling for) the common factor, there is an effect of complex language when using star ratings on variable 4.

That is, freeing an intercept in 1 of 4 experimental groups implies an interaction between wording and response format.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
